headline: Medium-risk pair: shared content flow can enable prompt injection and cascading errors; no direct evidence of shared storage or residency mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and uses MCP/browser/network egress; rasa consumes conversational text/voice and can expose outputs through chat channels. A plausible bridge exists if draw-io content is forwarded into rasa or copied into a shared channel, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded into agent_b chat messages or intents, prompt-injection content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF a shared MCP or messaging bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled document text can traverse without provenance checks.
mitigations: Disable any automatic forwarding from agent_a to agent_b.
Add a provenance tag to all agent_a outputs before they reach agent_b.
Require human review for any document-derived text before it enters rasa.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for agent_a where possible.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a handles PDFs, text files, images, and diagram XML and requests API keys/environment variables; agent_b handles text/voice and sends to allowlisted channels. If they share a workspace or message bus, sensitive document content from agent_a can leak into agent_b outputs or external chat surfaces. No shared filesystem is documented, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share files, transcripts, or a queue, document contents can be exposed in agent_b responses.
IF agent_a processes secrets-bearing documents and agent_b relays them to external chat APIs, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials for each agent.
Block agent_b from receiving raw document attachments.
Redact secrets from agent_a outputs before handoff.
Turn off logging of full prompts and attachments.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and broad network egress; agent_b does not support multiple instances and has allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces such as shared filesystem, git, or database access, so a direct write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty stays low because the conflict pathway is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource, concurrent updates can conflict.
IF an orchestrator adds shared state without locking, race conditions can appear.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same ticket or file.
Serialize any shared-resource updates.
Use per-agent credentials for mutable services.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and agent_b is a dialogue system that can act on conversational inputs. If agent_b treats agent_a's generated text or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade from document interpretation into customer-facing responses. The profiles do not show verification gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a summaries are passed into agent_b without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as final customer replies, downstream mistakes become visible externally.
mitigations: Require a human check before agent_a outputs reach agent_b.
Mark agent_a content as draft, not authoritative.
Add a verification step that compares outputs to source documents.
Limit agent_b to templated responses when using agent_a content.
requires-engineering: implement citation-backed answer validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not specify regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII, nor any residency mismatch. agent_a handles documents and API keys, while agent_b handles text/voice and allowlisted messaging APIs, but no compliance breach is provable from the profiles alone. The other agent is not cited beyond noting the absence of a mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through both agents, compliance review is required.
IF retention policies differ after deployment, stored transcripts may violate policy.
mitigations: Classify data before routing between agents.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Restrict logs to minimal metadata.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
